options: Grid requires media queries, flex doesn't
Grid is older, flex is newer
explanation: Flexbox is a 1D layout system (axis-based); CSS Grid is a 2D system with rows and columns.
An absolutely positioned element is positioned relative to its nearest ancestor with position != static; here, .parent (position: relative) is the containing block.
Modern flexbox (display: flex on parent) is more reliable than float clearing; if stuck with floats, overflow: hidden or ::after work.

question:
When will a z-index declaration have no effect?
```css
.box { z-index: 100; }
```
explanation: z-index only works on positioned elements (position != static); z-index: 100 is ignored if position is not set.

question:
What CSS rule creates a new stacking context without changing position or z-index?
```css
.layer { position: static; opacity: 0.99; }
```
explanation: opacity with a value less than 1 creates a new stacking context, isolating the element's z-index from siblings.

options: Relative stays in flow, absolute doesn't
explanation: position: relative keeps the element in document flow (still takes up space); position: absolute removes it, and top/left position relative to containing block.
For absolutely positioned elements, left: 0 and right: 0 with margin: 0 auto centers horizontally within the containing block.
A transform on a parent creates a containing block for fixed children; they position relative to the transformed parent, not the viewport.

options: Display table is ignored in flex
explanation: Children of flex containers become flex items; their display value determines internal layout, but they still flex as items in the parent.
position: sticky only sticks within its scrolling ancestor; if parent has overflow: hidden and doesn't scroll, sticky has no effect.
